frontier.hypothesis: The v0/v1 register-coloring swap (raw-load pseudo grabs $v0 via local-alloc before the cross-block AND-result pseudo is even considered by global-alloc) is still the entire visible residual pattern and needs a lever that stops the raw-load temp from being treated as purely block-local.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 pass ordering: local-alloc.c runs before global.c; local-alloc greedily assigns the lowest free hardreg (ascending default order, no MIPS REG_ALLOC_ORDER override) to any pseudo confined to one basic block, before global-alloc ever processes pseudos that cross blocks.
frontier.next_probe: Try restructuring so the arm-value variable (v0, used inside/after the if/else) is NOT itself one pseudo crossing the branch -- e.g. genuinely separate per-arm locals merged through a mechanism other than one shared block-scoped v0. Not yet attempted this session.

frontier.mechanism: Unknown -- H5's own dump read ruled out the coloring swap as the cause but did not identify the actual cause.

frontier.hypothesis: A single equal-priority scheduler tie in block3 (sb $v0,0x6($s0) vs addu $a0,$s0,$zero ordering, identified in session 2) may resolve itself for free once the coloring issue is fixed.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2's list scheduler (sched.c rank_for_schedule) picks between two ready, mutually-independent instructions by priority; a coloring fix upstream can shift RTL insn numbering/height enough to flip the tie-break outcome.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the register-normalized diff after any further coloring lever lands, to see if this tie resolves as a side effect before spending a dedicated session on it.
